summary: This work proposes an extensible 2D architecture for scaling fluxonium qubits using low-shunt-capacitance tunable couplers based on generalized flux-qubit circuits (quarton and fluxonium designs). The architecture addresses the capacitance loading problem by achieving coupling strengths $\sim250$–$500$ MHz with coupling capacitances $C_{qt} \approx 1.7$–$5.5$ fF (versus $3.5$–$12.2$ fF for transmon-based designs), enabling multiple connections in 2D grids while maintaining tunable control of plasmon interactions and suppression of spectator errors.
motivation: While individual fluxonium qubits have demonstrated gate fidelities exceeding 99.9% and coherence times into the millisecond regime, scaling beyond two qubits to 2D lattices requires addressable tunable couplers that do not compromise the small-footprint advantage of fluxonium qubits (typical shunt capacitance $\sim 20$ fF with charging energy $E_C/2\pi \sim 1$ GHz).
method: The authors leverage coupler designs with small shunt capacitances ($C_{TC} \approx 15$ fF) based on $N$-junction arrays: quarton circuits with $\gamma/N \sim 0.92$ ($N=8$) and fluxonium couplers with $\gamma/N \lesssim 10^{-2}$ ($N \sim 100$, where $\gamma = E_{J,a}/E_{J,c}$). Tunable plasmon interactions ($|1\rangle \leftrightarrow |2\rangle$) between qubits are realized by flux-biasing the coupler to modulate its detuning from the qubit transition, achieving sub-100 ns MAP-based CZ gates with DRAG pulse correction.
result: CZ gate fidelities comparable to isolated two-qubit systems are demonstrated with spectator-induced frequency shifts suppressed below 1 kHz and gate errors below $10^{-5}$ when spectator couplers are turned off; the quarton coupler reaches conditional frequency shifts of $\sim 55$ MHz with $50$-ns gate times, while the fluxonium coupler achieves $\sim 43$ MHz shifts, both with manageable coupler-induced Purcell errors ($\sim 10^{-4}$ level for non-computational state lifetimes of $\sim 10$ µs).
